title: 4 Best Electric Toothbrushes, From Basic to Fully Featured
metaDescription: The best electric toothbrushes for value, sensitive gums, extra features and travel, with honest limitations for each.
lede: Most people get the biggest benefit from a brush with a two-minute timer and a pressure sensor. Extra features are nice but optional. These picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.

products.name: Oral-B Pro 1000 Electric Toothbrush
products.bestFor: anyone switching from a manual brush
products.blurb: A long-running basic oscillating-rotating brush with the two features that matter most: a two-minute timer with 30-second pacing, and a pressure sensor.
strengths: Covers the essentials at a low price
limitations: Basic charging stand and no travel case

products.name: Philips Sonicare 4100 Power Toothbrush
products.bestFor: sensitive gums and people who prefer a gentler feel
products.blurb: An entry-level sonic brush with a slim handle, a pressure sensor, a quadrant timer and a reminder when it's time to replace the brush head (Philips spec).
strengths: Quieter and gentler feel than oscillating brushes
limitations: Replacement heads cost more than many Oral-B heads
Feel takes some getting used to

products.name: Oral-B iO Series 5 Electric Toothbrush
products.searchQuery: Oral-B iO Series 5 rechargeable electric toothbrush
products.bestFor: people who want app guidance and a quieter Oral-B
products.blurb: Part of Oral-B's iO range, which uses a magnetic drive for a smoother, quieter feel than older Oral-B brushes, plus a smart pressure sensor and app support.
strengths: Smoother and quieter than classic Oral-B brushes
limitations: iO heads only fit iO handles and cost more

products.name: quip Electric Toothbrush
products.blurb: A slim sonic brush with a built-in two-minute timer and a cover that doubles as a mirror mount. Simple, light and easy to pack.
limitations: Gentler, less powerful than rechargeable flagships

howWeChose: We prioritised a two-minute timer and a pressure sensor, the features most associated with better brushing habits.
Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
We factored in the ongoing cost of replacement heads, not just the handle.

faqs.q: How often should I replace the brush head?
faqs.a: Manufacturers and dental bodies generally recommend about every three months, or sooner if the bristles are frayed.

faqs.q: Is an electric toothbrush better than a manual one?
faqs.a: Many people brush more thoroughly with one, thanks to timers and pressure sensors. A manual brush used well for two minutes twice a day can also be effective. Ask your dentist what suits you.
